sources.title: Arie Lawrence Hersh - Cuyahoga naturalization card
sources.description: Original card image inspected and reading CONFIRMED (Lane B, Sept 27, 2026): 'NAME: ARIE - LAWRENCE - HERSH; SUBJECT OF: ISRAEL; date nat 8/11/61; born 6/1/25; Remarks: Name changed as part of nat. from: ARIE - LARRY - HERSH KOVITZ'; signed Arie Lawrence Hersh. Office no. 201619; certificate no. 8195469; naturalized August 11, 1961, U.S. District Court, Cleveland. 'Subject of: Israel' shows Israeli citizenship at naturalization - the via-Israel route is inference-level. The underlying petition and birth record remain unchecked.

sources.title: Szymon Warszavski - Social Security NUMIDENT index
sources.description: Indexed NUMIDENT extraction displayed on authenticated FamilySearch page; no underlying SS-5 image available. Gives birth April 1, 1918 in Warsaw, Poland; June 1963 social program application; Cleveland; death July 18, 1995; parents indexed as Joseph Warszavski and Rochel Goldberg. Same death date as original 1995 obituary supports identity. Parent spellings and birth details require original SS-5 or other independent record.

sources.title: Elka Kagan Zelkind - Social Security NUMIDENT index
sources.description: Authenticated indexed page screenshot inspected; no original SS-5 image. Elka Kagan Zelkind (alias Elka Kagan Kaga), birth November 12, 1913 in indexed "Bubruysk, Soviet Union" (the Soviet Union label is anachronistic for 1913), April 29, 1981 application, Cleveland, death March 14, 2005. Indexed parents Isac Kaga and Tsilya Gershon. Ohio death index gives paternal surname Kogan; Kaga/Kagan/Kogan are unverified variants, not merged into a legal maiden name.

sources.title: Zion Memorial Park burial register - Warszawski and Zelkind surname results
sources.publisher: Zion Memorial Park, Bedford Heights, Ohio
sources.description: Cemetery-operated last-name search inspected September 25, 2026. Warszawski: BERTHA interred Nov 29, 2016, Z6 row 1 grave 58. Zelkind: ELKA interred March 16, 2005, Z6 row 4 grave 110; MORDUKH interred Sept 25, 1996, Z6 row 6 grave 110; GAIL interred Feb 1, 2013, Z6 row 4 grave 111. Interment dates, not death dates; cemetery cautions typos/human error. Cemetery alone does not prove Gail’s kinship; Mordukh’s separate 1996 original notice identifies her as his daughter. Hersh search: ILEEN interred May 24, 2009, Z3 row 1 grave 34; LAWRENCE interred Jan 3, 2012, Z3 row 1 grave 35; duplicate Jan 5 RESERVE line at same grave is not a separate burial.

Born Chust (he spells it C-H-U-S-T), Czechoslovakia, June 1925; town of 35-40,000 with 8-10,000 Jews and about half a dozen synagogues. 'Ideal' childhood: affluent family (father's lumber + wine businesses), sports, movies, Carpathian summer vacations; cheder + Czech elementary + Hungarian gymnasium (~9 years schooling from 1931, forced out as a Jew); home language Yiddish, plus Hungarian/Czech/local Russian; area-wide BETAR youth leader; read Gone with the Wind in four languages.

HIS OWN TESTIMONY (1984): 'I had four sisters. And we were five kids. I was the only boy... Three were young. And they perished with my parents.' - FIVE children, Larry the OLDEST. This CONFLICTS with the family account 'part of a differing family total (original children/siblings wording needs checking)' recorded earlier; his own first-person testimony weighs heavier; conflict kept visible.
facts.note: Family-account 'a differing family total (wording unverified)' vs his own 'five kids' - testimony favored, both preserved.

facts.value: 1938: won a fully-paid place at a Prague school for talented youngsters (engineering track; ticket + instructions sent). His PATERNAL GRANDMOTHER went to the rabbi ('he'll eat treyf, no Shabbos, no tefillin'); pressure forced his father to cancel it.

Late 1942: the Zionist organization chose him for one of Khust's FOUR Palestine certificates. His mother objected ('After all, you're the big macher... it will look like you're taking for yourself'); he offered it to his younger sister, she refused that too - she wanted the family together. He gave it away. The four who left survived and are in Israel. 'The paradox of it is the ones who left, they all survived.'

1944 (he says 1943 - see date_conflict note): Khust ghetto. He organized food-collection wagons house-to-house during move-in; the Judenrat man addressed him by his Jewish name LEIBE; the Gestapo chief interrogated him (tested his German); warned by his father's Hungarian-policeman acquaintance of an arrest order, his father obtained him a legitimate (bribed) Hungarian ARMY CALL-UP signed by COLONEL KELETY (K-E-L-E-T-Y - later a recognized Righteous Gentile; his son was writing a book in Budapest as of 1984). On a Budapest trip he obtained two blank escape 'passports' - given to a young couple who survived in Palestine.
facts.note: He dates the ghetto to 1943; known Khust chronology (ghetto Apr-May 1944) + his own Shavuot anchor favor 1944. Conflict visible.

facts.value: Hungarian labor service at NAGYBANYA (yellow armband, own clothes): organized a 'hard core' group; smuggled a wagon of bread (hidden under hay) to the starving local ghetto - the GENERAL caught him and looked the other way ('next time don't be a dumb Jew and let yourself be caught'), later praised 'job well done' (Larry stayed in contact with the general's son). Friend LEONARD FOX (living in Cleveland in 1984) took 45 lashes on a later bread run; Larry escaped over the fields, returned to the ghetto at night - and was deported with its liquidation the next morning.

Deported by freight car (80-100 per car, 5 days, water only) to AUSCHWITZ, arriving 'two days before Shavuot' - the Shavuot calendar anchors this to 26 MAY 1944 (he said '1943'; conflict resolved toward 1944, kept visible). Mengele conducted the selection; Larry said he was 17, sent right. Prisoner number 8485 (as stated; once transcribed '845'). Learned a sister was alive across the wire; under a week in camp, then swapped blocks to join the Warsaw transport after hearing his FATHER and an uncle had been sent there.
facts.note: Date conflict (his '1943' vs the Shavuot anchor + Khust deportation chronology) resolved visibly toward May 1944.

facts.value: Warsaw camp ON THE RUINS OF THE GHETTO (KZ Warschau): cleaned bricks from bombed buildings, loaded trains for the Russian front. Reunited with his father after six weeks. Saw the Judenrat sign; translated for a guard the blood-written Yiddish on the Anielewicz-bunker wall: 'we were betrayed, remember us.' Assigned to clean the killer-dog cages (German shepherds) - the kitchen food he earned kept his father, uncle and friends alive for weeks. Witnessed SS immolating bound, gagged prisoners stacked 'like wood' - 'the horror of being stripped of the ability to even scream at one's own pain.'

August 1944: camp dissolved ahead of the Russian advance; ~10,000 marched out (2 days standing without food/water, then the salt-herring ration); fewer than 8,000 reached Kutno (8-10 days; prisoners who stooped to drink had their necks crushed; two days lying in mud); cattle train to DACHAU - about 2,000 survived. His father and uncle made it (uncle beaten on the head).

Dachau (3-4 days) -> LANDSBERG Lager 7 (underground earth huts; typhus quarantine) -> KAUFERING Lager 4; night construction for Baustelle Holzmann (underground airfields). His father, 48 and broken ('water in their knees'), was taken away with the uncle and the older generation - never seen again; Larry assumes he perished at Dachau.

Early spring 1945: typhus, 28 days unfed/untreated (an SS guard's rifle at his head - the second guard said 'leave him, he's finished anyhow; save the bullet'). May 1945: evacuation train; the US Air Force disabled the locomotive; a German army train used the prisoners as a human shield; Larry and TWO others - the last three of his eight-man hard core - escaped through forest to American-occupied SCHWABHAUSEN. He weighed 38 kilos. A month in an army hospital; an older survivor (~50, six years in camps) died of a heart attack beside him after liberation.

His mother is named indirectly: the Jewish US Army doctor who visited the hospital tracked down his uncle by phone from Cleveland - the message ran 'Leibi Hersch... your sister's son, LEAH'. So his mother was LEAH, sister of the Cleveland uncle JANOWITZ (transcript spelling; the USHMM summary renders 'Yanowicz'). Mother's side had two brothers and two sisters in America; his father's side had one brother in California (visited Khust in 1933).

June 1945: Prague; learned from hometown girls that his youngest-but-one sister was ALIVE, liberated at Bergen-Belsen (British zone). Budapest: recruited by JOEL BRAND (of the Eichmann negotiations; Larry had seen Eichmann in Budapest in 1943 without knowing who he was); Irgun member; BRICHA border-guide 1945-47; sailed Italy->Palestine early 1947 (10 days); hunted by the British, smuggled out to CYPRUS hidden among oranges/grapefruit; France; Germany Feb 1948; returned to Israel ON THE ALTALENA; eight years in the Israeli army through the 1956 war.

1956: emigrated to CLEVELAND to his sister (already there since 1947, sponsored by uncle Janowitz, who paid her way and took her in 'like one of their own daughters') - he stayed first with her, then three months with the uncle. Met his wife in Cleveland (American-born, parents born in the US). Joined the MARMAROSHER Jewish Temple on Lancashire (Hungarian congregation) - the USHMM summary instead says B'nai Jeshurun; variant kept. Three daughters by 1984 (one pre-med in college, one starting college, one in high school) = Lori, Susanne, Marcy.

The interview corroborates June 1925 birth: liberated May 1945 'one month before my 20th birthday... I was born in June.' (Resolves the earlier note doubting the 1925 date on the naturalization card.)
He saw EICHMANN in Budapest in 1943 ('I saw an SS officer... Eichmann didn't mean nothing to me at the time').
